news.title: Lekjaa reveals the outline of Morocco's project for the 2030 World Cup: a plan that goes beyond the stadiums
news.lede: What the cameras don't seeMorocco's World Cup ambition reaches far beyond match venues and stadiums ready to welcome teams and fans. It has become a sweeping development project, one designed to redraw the country's map of infrastructure and transport while spreading the benefits across every region of the Kingdom, part of extraordinary preparations to host the 2030 edition.Fouzi Lekjaa, president of the Royal Moroccan Football Federation, insists the Kingdom's bid rests on decades of groundwork. That developmental path began in the late 1990s and has now been crowned with the honour of staging the 2030 tournament.Speaking in comments reported by the Moroccan website "Hespress" , Lekjaa described the coming edition as exceptional.

news.title: Malaysia kick off FIFA U-15 World Cup campaign with 3-1 win over Dominica
news.lede: Malaysia took a 2-0 lead through Aqheef Haiqal Koko's opening goal in the 12th minute before Anas Suffiyan Arif doubled the advantage seven minutes later. KUALA LUMPUR : The national Under-15 squad opened their Group H campaign in the 2026 FIFA Under-15 World Cup and Festival with a 3-1 victory over Dominica in Baku, Azerbaijan today. Dominica reduced the deficit through a penalty in the 28th minute, but Amirul Faris Azlan sealed the win for coach P. Maniam's side with a third goal in the 39th minute.

news.title: Singapore finish 141st in inaugural FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival
news.lede: Singapore forward Adryan Alfian taking on players in their 9-0 win over the British Virgin Islands in the Tier E knockout stage of the inaugural FIFA Under-15 World Cup and Festival. PHOTO: FOOTBALL ASSOCIATION OF SINGAPORE. SINGAPORE – After playing 10 matches in seven days, Singapore emerged 141st out of 189 teams at the inaugural FIFA Under-15 World Cup and Festival in Baku, Azerbaijan. The Cubs beat Eswatini 4-1 on Oct 30 in their final match of the eight-a-side competition played across 20-minute halves.

news.title: FIFA to visit potential 2030 World Cup host cities in November and December
news.lede: FIFA will carry out a series of visits to candidate host cities in Spain, Portugal and Morocco in November and December as part of the venue selection process for the 2030 World Cup, world football's governing body said on Tuesday. A FIFA delegation will visit candidate cities and stadiums in all three host countries to assess their suitability to host games. FIFA has yet to confirm which venues will be included, and has not announced where the World Cup final will be held, with Spain and Morocco battling to hold football's biggest match. Visits are planned for Agadir, Casablanca, Fez, Marrakech, Rabat and Tangier in Morocco; Lisbon and Porto in Portugal; and Barcelona, Bilbao, Las Palmas, Madrid, San Sebastian, Seville and Zaragoza in Spain.
